from_notes: In Andhra Pradesh, inflation fell from 7.57% in 2022–23 to 1.39% in 2025–26.
x: The Union Economic Survey 2025-26 put Andhra Pradesh's inflation at 1.39% in 2025-26, down from 7.57% in 2022-23 (national 1.72%). 1.11%, 3.84% and 1.95% are the 2026-27 revenue, fiscal and primary deficits as % of GSDP. (The figure comes from the Union Economic Survey, not from AP's own Socio-Economic Survey.)
source: Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 magazine p.98 ('Declining Inflation in Telugu States', according to the Economic Survey 2025-26)
evidence: Deccan Chronicle headline 'AP inflation drops sharply to 1.39 in 2025-26: Economic Survey of India' (web search)

from_notes: ₹6,000 crore allocated for the development of Amaravati ... ₹6,105 crore for the Polavaram Project.
x: Polavaram got ₹6,105 crore in the AP Budget 2026-27. ₹4,765 crore is Tribal Welfare and ₹4,000 crore NTR Vaidya Seva; Thalliki Vandanam got ₹8,456 crore (PRS), so ₹9,668 crore is a distractor.
source: PRS AP Budget Analysis 2026-27 (prsindia.org, 11 Mar 2026) p.3 (Polavaram ₹6,105 crore, Thalliki Vandanam ₹8,456 crore); Praveen CA-360 Feb 2026 p.60
evidence: PRS AP Budget Analysis 2026-27 PDF: 'Rs 8,456 crore has been allocated to the Thalliki Vandanam scheme' (old explanation said ₹9,668 crore)

from_notes: Rs. 32,308 crore for School Education Department of which Rs.1,500 crore is proposed for overhauling the infrastructure in public schools
x: School Education got ₹32,308 crore, the largest department allocation. Health, Medical and Family Welfare got ₹19,306 crore, Thalliki Vandanam ₹8,456 crore (PRS) and Tribal Welfare ₹4,765 crore (₹11,118 crore is Social Welfare).
source: AP Budget Speech 2026-27 p.10 (₹32,308 crore School Education), p.22 (₹19,306 crore Health); PRS AP Budget Analysis 2026-27 p.3 (Thalliki Vandanam ₹8,456 crore)

x: ₹34,350 crore was reported for BC Welfare in the AP Budget 2026-27 (the BC component across departments is ₹51,021 crore). Social Welfare got ₹11,118 crore, School Education ₹32,308 crore and Minority Welfare ₹2,956 crore.
source: The News Minute, 'Andhra Pradesh presents Rs 3.32 lakh crore Budget for 2026-27' (web search); AP Budget Speech 2026-27 p.21 (BC component ₹51,021 crore)
evidence: Deccan Chronicle: BC welfare department ₹23,324.44 crore
AP Budget Speech p.21: BC component ₹51,021 crore
dispute: Most reports and the app: BC Welfare ₹34,350 crore (The News Minute). The BC Welfare Department proper is given as ₹23,650.88 crore (South First) or ₹23,324.44 crore (Deccan Chronicle); either way the answer is BC Welfare.

x: P4 stands for Public–Private–People Partnership, the Swarna Andhra @2047 model for zero poverty, which brings in Margadarsis (mentors) to help poor families. The other expansions are made-up distractors.
source: AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.302 (9.6 P4 approach, zero poverty); CARE APPSC Feb 2026 p.14 (P4: 'People-Public-Private Partnership', Margadarsis, Bangaru Mitras)
dispute: Most books and the app: Public–Private–People Partnership. The SES 2024-25 heading (p.302) writes 'Public-People Philanthropic Partnership' and CARE (Feb 2026 p.14) 'People-Public-Private Partnership'; all are the same P4 zero-poverty model.
